limitations: All 34 editorial requirements of four publisher identities reviewed for authored teaching; whole-chapter readiness is not inferred.
Original observations and diagrams are invented teaching models, not real microscopy or practical experiments. No learner, human examiner or active-template certification.

requirements.judgement: Plant synthesis using light versus animal digested nutrients assessed; minerals are not conflated with energy or organic food.
Dark-grown seed/storage context distinguishes cellular respiration from lungs and photosynthesis.
Undigested fibre versus metabolic urea assessed by origin, with carbon dioxide explanation; excretion and egestion not conflated.
Directional seedling change linked to light without a process label cue in the practice.
Rooted organism movement demonstrated without claiming whole-organism locomotion.
Invented changing external/stable-range internal temperatures assessed; limited evidence cannot prove mechanisms or exact constancy.
Juvenile/lineage contrast assesses absence of current reproduction without diagnosing non-life.
Dry-mass increase, new leaf function and viable offspring independently separate growth, development and reproduction.
Multicellularity and leaf photosynthesis are compared with specialised roots lacking chloroplasts; unfamiliar correction retains organism versus cell context.
Plant cellulose, starch and sucrose are explicitly corrected in practice; fungal chitin and glycogen are separately compared.
Maize and herbaceous beans are classified as plants, distinguishing examples from kingdoms without photograph identification.
Unfamiliar R uses multicellularity, absent walls/chloroplasts and organic feeding together to identify animal organisation.
Practice qualifies nervous coordination and locomotion as typical rather than universal observed behaviour; glycogen alone cannot separate animal from fungus.
Humans/mosquitoes are classified in practice and housefly/human comparison is worked; mammal/insect labels remain within animals.
Chitin walls, absence of photosynthesis and possible glycogen storage are assessed against plant and animal alternatives.
Original labelled hypha/mycelium/nuclei drawing checked; practice contrasts thread network and many nuclei with single-celled yeast.
Unfamiliar dead seed substrate requires enzymes out, extracellular digestion and soluble products in; swallowing and enzyme absorption errors corrected.
Mucor and yeast are independently classified as fungi; worked yeast/bacterium correction and thread/one-cell comparison prevent single-cell overgeneralisation.
Single nucleated S contrasted with a similarly microscopic prokaryotic cell; cell size or number alone cannot establish the group.
Practice contrasts organic feeding Amoeba and photosynthetic Chlorella, retaining within-protoctist chloroplast variability.
Practice distinguishes Plasmodium protoctist pathogen from mosquito insect vector without conflating the transmission role with the causative agent.
Unfamiliar microscopic single-cell isolate is classified using circular DNA outside a nucleus and several cell structures.
Original A/B/C label endpoints visually checked against outer wall, inner membrane and cytoplasm; practice identifies all three.
Practice identifies D circular chromosome and E plasmid; worked case rejects missing plasmids as evidence of an animal or lack of genetic information.
Invented mixed photosynthetic/organic-feeding isolates assess some versus most nutrition modes without making nutrition universal.
Named rod-shaped Lactobacillus bulgaricus and yoghurt production assessed as separate shape, name and use facts.
Spherical Pneumococcus/pneumonia assessed with limits of unknown-specimen shape inference and counterexamples to universal bacterial pathogenicity.
Disease-causing ability assessed separately from microscopic size, organism group and location; useful examples refute a universal harm claim.
Practice supplies disease-causing fungus, Pneumococcus, Plasmodium and influenza; the four agent groups must be identified separately.
Non-cellular coat/genome particle contrasted with bacterial organisation; unfamiliar 1.5 micrometre/75 nanometre measurements independently give 20, not a picture-size inference.
Host-cell-only reproduction is explained and assessed; practice corrects infection across major groups versus any one virus infecting all species.
Two original generic shapes visually reviewed with protein-coat and internal genome labels; practice rejects DNA alone as proof of a cell and explanation distinguishes DNA OR RNA.
Worked and unfamiliar practice require TMV infection, disrupted chloroplast formation and discoloured leaf sequence, without colour-only diagnosis.
Influenza/flu and HIV/AIDS associations assessed, distinguishing a virus name from disease/syndrome and avoiding symptom diagnosis.
